courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Introduction to Theatre
courses.description: An introduction to the art and concepts of theatre through a study of modern and historical theories of dramatic structure, playwriting, directing, design, and acting. Attendance of live theatre required. CSU/UC

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Theatre and Cultural Diversity
courses.description: Through lectures, readings, documentaries, and films, the class will illustrate the contributions of diverse cultures to the fabric of American Theatre and entertainment. Focus will be upon the influence of Latino American, Asian American, African American cultures, LGBTQ Americans and the under recognized influence of women playwrights. The class will also present and illustrate alternative theatre viewpoints from political and experimental perspectives. The student will be asked to discuss, react and compare aspects of these diverse theatres/genres, including costume, scenic, lighting and make-up design, and acting style. CSU

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Acting Fundamentals
courses.description: A study of acting involving the development of acting techniques, styles, and disciplines. Provides theory and practical experience with varied characterizations. Emphasizes individual growth and acquired skills necessary to the acting craft. A combination of Theatre Arts 110, 111, and 118 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Intermediate Acting
courses.description: Further study in the art of acting for the stage, investigating in-depth character study, role portrayal, special problems, and personal technique. Acting skills developed through use of exercises, monologues, and scenes from contemporary theatre. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Acting for the Camera II
courses.description: An intermediate and immersive on-camera experience in which the student will have opportunities to practice skills and techniques in several styles of camera production: movie/TV narrative drama, comedy, and reality TV. The material from these performances is edited, screened, and discussed. CSU/UC
review: Department inferred from unique subject mapping within this college; verify current ownership

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Fundamentals of Scene Study
courses.description: A continued study for the beginning actor in the preparation and presentation of scenes from modern comedies, the plays of William Shakespeare, and plays from influential playwrights such as Anton Chekov and Henrik Ibsen. Students prepare scenes with partners for performance and critique. A combination of Theatre Arts 110, 111, and 118 may be taken a maximum of four enrollments. CSU/UC

courses.subject: THEA
courses.title: Musical Theatre History
courses.description: This course explores the history of the uniquely American art form that is musical theatre from its early development in the colonial period to the present time. Emphasis will be placed on the chronological examination of various musical theatre productions. Students will learn how the composers, librettists, lyricists, choreographers, directors, and designers contributed to the formation and the popularity of musical theatre as it exists today. CSU/UC

notes: CU0002 is parsed explicitly; unrecognized catalog layouts are not guessed.
Crosswalk ownership is college-aware; ambiguous ownership remains flagged instead of silently assigned.
CU0321 last-offered data is a planning signal only and does not determine curriculum currency.
DO NOT SCHEDULE rooms are owner-only when a matching owner division is present; they are not campuswide rooms.
Shared portal writes are revalidated server-side; browser-calculated totals are not trusted.
Local database mode writes proposals to SQLite with revision history and stores per-department draft workspaces; static HTML is preview-only for database actions.
Department draft workspaces are isolated by term/college/division/department so switching scope does not destroy unfinished work.
2026-27 credit default is Standardized Attendance Accounting; open-entry/open-exit credit remains Actual Hours / Positive Attendance.
Faculty load caps/factors are configurable planning values, not a contractual certification.
Pathway membership comes only from a confirmed administrator-provided mapping; it is never inferred from course title, TOP code, or division.
Imported existing bookings are a snapshot at generation time, not a live Ad Astra/Colleague connection; regenerate after refreshing the booking export.
Empty optional booking/pathway CSV files are ignored with import warnings; malformed or headerless files produce a clear validation error instead of a raw csv traceback.
RG0547 prepopulation maps prior dates by relative term week + weekday; previous CRNs are retained only as a reference and are never reused as current-term identifiers.
Block schedule alignment is advisory. The planner suggests approved windows and permits documented exceptions rather than blocking CTE/long-format schedules.
Department-chair modality labels are translated to scheduler/Colleague codes from the imported DE coding reference when available.
